newsitem.title: CANADA: Midland says letter not bona fide offer.
newsitem.headline: Midland says letter not bona fide offer.

text.p: Midland Walwyn Inc does not regard a letter sent by the Canadian Alliance of Individual Investors as a legitimate offer for the company, its general counsel said on Wednesday.

The letter, addressed to Midland Walwyn chief executive Robert Schultz from CAII executive director Stephen Handler, said an anonymous U.S. financial services house was interested in acquiring Midland in a deal that would give shareholders in the range of C$15 a share. Handler, head of the advocacy group for retail investors, told Reuters the U.S. brokerage was Travelers Group Inc's Smith Barney.
"We have I believe probably the same letter that you do and it's our view that it's not a bona fide offer," said Brad Doney, general counsel for Midland Walwyn.
Smith Barney agreed there was no basis for the report.
"I can absolutely deny this," Smith Barney spokesman Bob Connor said in a telephone interview.

Takeover speculation about Midland Walwyn, whose Midland Walwyn Capital is the last major Canadian brokerage not affiliated with a Canadian bank, has persisted since Royal Bank of Canada last year acquired Richardson Greenshields of Canada Ltd, the only other big independent dealer.
But Doney said Midland Walwyn's strategy was to maintain its independence. He said rumors of other approaches to were false.
Last October, Schultz said the broker was not for sale and suggested the probability of a hostile takeover bid was low.

"The fact is we are not for sale. We are fully committed to independence," Schultz told an analysts' meeting last autumn. Schultz said it would be difficult for someone to launch a hostile bid without support from management, which owns about 18 percent of the shares.
The CAII letter said: "The acquirer who wishes to remain anonymous at the moment does not wish to launch a hostile takeover bid for MWI."
Mutual fund company Mackenzie Financial Inc is another major shareholder with an equity stake of just more than 20 percent.
Midland Walwyn shares jumped to a 52-week high of 13.50 on the Toronto Stock Exchange today before pulling back to trade up 1 at 13.15.
